summary: Patch correctly prevents roc_curve from emitting a first threshold >1 when scores are probability estimates by prepending 1 instead of thresholds[0]+1, resolving the reported issue without regressing the decision-function case (max>1 keeps old +1 behavior). Approach is slightly heuristic and lacks an explanatory comment, but is functionally sound and mergeable.

issues.description: Inferring 'this is a probability estimate' from thresholds.max() <= 1 is implicit/heuristic; a decision_function whose outputs happen to fall <=1 also takes this branch. Result is still a valid (0,0) sentinel point, so no correctness break, but the abstraction is a bit fragile compared to a sentinel like np.inf.
New conditional adds no comment explaining why the <=1 case prepends 1 (probability-clip rationale). A one-line comment would aid maintainability.
When thresholds[0] == 1 exactly, prepending 1 creates a duplicate leading threshold (non-strictly-decreasing). Harmless for curve semantics but slightly untidy.
